basic_information.short_title: Plebiscite Requirement for Datu Sinsuat Balabaran, amended
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 5 OF BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 54, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ACT CREATING THE MUNICIPALITY OF DATU SINSUAT BALABARAN IN THE PROVINCE OF MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or one newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Changes who votes on whether the Municipality of Datu Sinsuat Balabaran is created. The plebiscite is now held in “the political units directly affected”, not only in the barangays being carved out.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: BAA 54 confined the plebiscite to the barangays leaving the mother municipality. The Organic Law requires ratification by the political units directly affected — wording this amendment restores, and which is generally understood to include the municipality losing the territory.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The franchise for the ratification vote widens. The 60-day deadline and the requirement of a majority of votes cast are unchanged.
who_will_be_affected: Voters in the barangays that would form Datu Sinsuat Balabaran
Voters in the mother municipality, who on the amended wording are within the units directly affected
COMELEC, which must call and conduct the plebiscite on the wider basis
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The vote on creating Datu Sinsuat Balabaran is held in the political units directly affected — a wider franchise than the original act, which polled only the departing barangays.
in_practice: The plebiscite is 'called for the purpose in the political units directly affected'
Ratification still requires a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters
It must still be held within 60 days after approval of the Act
Everything else in BAA 54 — the barangays, the seat of government, the appointed first officials, the ₱2.5 million monthly assistance — is untouched

for_specific_groups.Voters in the departing barangays: You still vote, and a majority of votes cast still decides.
for_specific_groups.Voters in the mother municipality: The amended wording reaches the political units directly affected, which is ordinarily read to include the municipality losing the barangays.
for_specific_groups.COMELEC: The plebiscite must be called on the wider basis rather than confined to the new municipality's barangays.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: At the plebiscite, whenever it is called.
what_you_can_do: Ask COMELEC which units are included in the plebiscite under the amended Section 5
Read this alongside BAA 54, which carries everything else about the new municipality
watch_out_for: 'The political units directly affected' is not defined in the act itself.
The 60-day clock runs from 'approval of the Act', and the amendment does not say whether that means the original creating act or this amending one.
The amendment does not say what happens to any plebiscite already held on the narrower basis.

key_terms_explained.Plebiscite: A vote of the people directly affected, required before a municipality can be created.
key_terms_explained.Political units directly affected: The local government units whose territory or composition the change alters — ordinarily read to include both the new unit and the one it is carved from.
key_terms_explained.Corporate existence: The point at which a municipality legally exists and can act.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Akhirah 11, 1446 / 12 December 2024, approved by the Chief Minister on 20 December 2024.

benefits.headline: A wider franchise for the vote that decides whether the municipality is created.

direct_benefits.benefit: A say in the plebiscite for the units directly affected, not only the departing barangays
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Voters in the affected local government units
direct_benefits.how_to_access: At the plebiscite called by COMELEC

indirect_benefits: Alignment with the Organic Law's own formulation of the ratification requirement
limitations: The act does not define which units are 'directly affected'.
It changes only the plebiscite provision; nothing else about the municipality.

for_citizens: None beyond voting in the plebiscite, which is a right rather than a duty.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections (COMELEC), which calls and conducts the plebiscite
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A resident of the mother municipality assumed they had no say in whether Datu Sinsuat Balabaran is created. Under the amended Section 5 the plebiscite is held in the political units directly affected, not only in the departing barangays.
A voter asks when the plebiscite happens. It must be held within 60 days after approval of the Act — though the amendment leaves it unclear which act that clock runs from.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 5 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 54 to read: the Municipality of Datu Sinsuat Balabaran shall acquire corporate existence upon ratification of its creation by a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters in a plebiscite called for the purpose in the political units directly affected, to be held within sixty (60) days after approval of the Act.
Section 4 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or one newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Voters in the affected local government units

related_legislation.related_note: Amends the plebiscite requirement in BAA 54. Passed alongside its twin — BAA 70 and BAA 71 make the identical change to the Datu Sinsuat Balabaran and Sheik Abas Hamza creating acts respectively.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. It governs only the plebiscite provision; the substance of the municipality's creation remains in BAA 54.

citizen_questions.a: Who votes. BAA 54 confined the plebiscite to the barangays being carved out; this amendment holds it in 'the political units directly affected', which is ordinarily read to include the mother municipality as well.
Not until the plebiscite ratifies it. This act changes the terms of that vote, not the result.

citizen_questions.q: When must the plebiscite be held?
citizen_questions.a: Within 60 days after approval of the Act. The amendment does not specify whether that clock runs from the original creating act or from this one.
No. The barangays, the seat of government, the appointed first officials and the ₱2.5 million monthly assistance all remain as enacted in BAA 54.
